item.title: Trump Meets Philippine Leader Before Flying to China
item.description:
Latest
Pinned
David E. Sanger and Katie Rogers
Reporting from Manila
Here’s the latest.
President Trump met with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines in Manila on Wednesday ahead of a flight to the Chinese city of Shenzhen, where he was expected to cap his whirlwind visit to Asia by meeting the leaders of China and Russia.
Mr. Marcos gave Mr. Trump a red-carpet welcome at the Malacañang Palace, complete with a military guard and a gun salute ahead of a bilateral meeting and banquet lunch. The U.S. delegation included Stephen Miller, the president’s new chief of staff, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
In his remarks to Mr. Marcos, Mr. Trump described the U.S.-Philippine relationship as “one of America’s oldest and most important alliances in the Pacific.”
Mr. Trump was expected to leave right after, having spent less than 24 hours in the Philippine capital. He briefly attended a gathering of Southeast Asian leaders and also met with the leaders of Japan, Australia and India on Tuesday.
In Shenzhen, the president is expected to attend the APEC economic summit, followed by a trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping of China and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia. Mr. Trump’s unpredictable agenda could include the future of American tariffs, nuclear arms control, the war in Ukraine and U.S. restrictions on advanced A.I. chips.
The brief itinerary in Asia appears to reflect Mr. Trump’s preferences. He dislikes big summits where he often is not the sole subject of attention. And he enjoys meeting with leaders of powerful nations — especially Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin, two authoritarian leaders he often talks about in admiring terms.
Mr. Trump will be meeting Mr. Xi for the third time this year, and a three-way meeting between China, Russia and the United States would be the first of its kind.
